adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Making `String getShortcut();` an abstract SPI method causes every already-deployed OAuth2 grant factory compiled against the prior interface to throw `AbstractMethodError` during the new factory's startup scan (P1, 100%).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33-36 in the interface file). This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of this interface that were compiled against the previous version without this method. When Keycloak starts up and scans for OAuth2GrantType providers via `getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` (as seen in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit), any factory implementation that doesn't have the `getShortcut()` method will throw `AbstractMethodError`. The diff confirms all built-in factories have been updated with the new method, but external/custom implementations would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — Because `encodeTokenId` accepts any `getShortcut()` result while the parser rejects `encodedContext.length() != 6`, a conforming extension with the interface-documented three-character grant shortcut emits token IDs this provider can never decode (P1, 100%).

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real inconsistency: the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` interface documentation says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder in `getTokenContextFromTokenId` strictly requires `encodedContext.length() != 6` (2 chars for sessionType + 2 chars for tokenType + 2 chars for grantType = 6 total). Looking at the actual implementations in the diff, all grant shortcuts are 2 characters (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', 'te', 'pg', 'ro', 'pc'), not 3 as the documentation suggests. If an extension follows the documented '3-letters' guidance, the encoded token ID would have 7 characters before the colon, causing the decoder to throw an IllegalArgumentException. This is a documentation/interface contract mismatch that could cause runtime failures for conforming extensions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Existing externally compiled OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers do not implement the newly abstract `getShortcut()` method, so startup invokes it and throws AbstractMethodError, preventing the server from accepting any token requests after an upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface has a new method `getShortcut()` added (lines in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java). This is a new abstract method in the interface. In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the code iterates over all OAuth2GrantType provider factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each one. If there are existing external/third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that were compiled against the old interface (without getShortcut()), they won't have this method implemented. When the code tries to call getShortcut() on such implementations, it will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime. This is a real backwards compatibility issue for custom grant type implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:105 — Removing the public `Context(Context)` constructor makes existing compiled grant extensions that clone their context fail with NoSuchMethodError during token handling, surfacing a raw endpoint failure instead of an OAuth error response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `Context(Context context)` copy constructor (lines 102-115 in the old code). This constructor was public and part of the `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class in the server-spi-private module, which is an SPI interface. Any external OAuth2 grant type extensions that were compiled against the previous version and use this copy constructor to clone context objects would fail at runtime with NoSuchMethodError when the method is called, since the constructor no longer exists. This is a binary compatibility break for existing extensions.
